## Data

This data comes from the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database, accessed through the 'tidyquant' package. It includes monthly employment rates for the United States, California, Oregon, Texas, and New York, from 1976 through 2026.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyquant)
library(knitr)
library(tidyverse)

unemp_raw <- read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")
head(unemp_raw)
#| message: false
source("ps2_script_Jackson.R")
```

## Wrangling

The following tables summarize key patterns in the unemployment data.

```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(unemp_summary, caption = "Mean, minimum, and maximum unemployment rate by region, full sample")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(unemp_recent_summary, caption = "Mean, minimum, and maximum unemployment rate by region, 2015-present")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(unemp_top_increases_no_covid, caption = "Five largest month-over-month increases in unemployment rate, excluding 2020")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(unemp_top_decreases_no_covid, caption = "Five largest month-over-month decreases in unemployment rate, excluding 2020")
```
